title: A Mathematica Package for Screw Calculus

sections.title: A Mathematica Package for Screw Calculus

scenes.title: Screw Toolkit
scenes.brief: A workbench of function "machines" — each a box with an input slot and output slot, drawn as icons (no words). SO(3) row: drop an orange ω arrow into the hat box → 3×3 skew tiles come out; vee box reverses it; exp box + θ slider outputs a spinning blue frame (lie.expSO3); axis box reads ω back from a frame (lie.logSO3). SE(3) row: R + p → 4×4 tiles (lie.homog); 4×4 → R and p (rotOf/transOf); twist ↔ 4×4 (hat/vee for twists); ad box → 6×6 tiles (lie.adjoint); screw box (pitch h, point q, direction ω) → twist (lie.screwAxis), with h = ∞ giving a pure slide; axis/pitch/magnitude boxes read a twist back into a gold axis line, pitch dial and magnitude bar. Point vs vector boxes append 1 or 0. Chaining boxes and seeing round-trips land back on the input (lime) is the game. Note: Crucible stores twists as (ω, v) while the book uses (v, ω); a swap toggle shows the reorder.

scenes.title: Robot From Twists
scenes.brief: Build an arm by dropping joint tokens onto a slate base: a revolute token needs a point q and an axis ω (gold line), a prismatic token needs a direction. Each token becomes a unit twist. Set the tool frame at home (pink). Joint sliders θᵢ (orange) drive the product of exponentials (kinematics.poeFK) and the pink tool moves; a Jacobian panel shows 6×n tile columns, each the current Ad-transformed joint twist (kinematics.spaceJacobian). Preset: a SCARA arm built from three vertical revolute axes at 0, l₁, l₁+l₂ and one vertical slide; its Jacobian shows the zero rows that reveal it can only yaw and move in x, y, z.

pages.summary: Appendix B describes a symbolic package implementing the screw calculus of Chapter 2, plus a companion for open-chain kinematics; availability notes; it uses homogeneous coordinates in R³.

atoms.idea: Appendix B title: a symbolic-math package for screw calculus.
A symbolic package implements every Chapter-2 operation on screws, twists and wrenches; with a companion package it computes open-chain manipulator kinematics symbolically and numerically [121].
atoms.feynman: A toolbox where every Chapter-2 trick is a ready-made gadget, plus an add-on kit for building arms.
atoms.visual: The workbench appears with two drawers: SO(3)/SE(3) gadgets (left) and arm-building gadgets (right); hovering a drawer shows thumbnails of the scenes each gadget powers.

atoms.idea: Availability notes: the source was distributed freely by file transfer with documentation; the authors disclaim responsibility for correctness or maintenance.
atoms.feynman: A free recipe card handed around, with a note saying "test the cake yourself".
atoms.visual: A small download badge on the workbench; Crucible's own src/core gadgets glow next to it with a lime "tested" check (the engine has its own test suite).

atoms.idea: The rest lists the functions and their arguments; it can double as a guide to writing a screw package in any language.
atoms.feynman: A parts list detailed enough to rebuild the machine in your own workshop.
atoms.visual: A side-by-side table view of gadget icons: left column the package gadget icon, right column the matching Crucible function chip (lie.hat, lie.expSO3, …); unmatched ones show a "NEW" chip.

atoms.idea: Subheading: using the package.
The package works in R³ and represents points, vectors and rigid motions in homogeneous coordinates (continues).
atoms.feynman: Every object gets an extra slot so one multiplication rule can move all of them.
atoms.visual: A teal point with a fourth slot "1" and an orange arrow with "0" sit on the bench next to a 4×4 tile matrix.

atoms.idea: Page 435

pages.summary: The package has two groups: SO(3) functions (hat, axis, skew exponential, vee) and SE(3) functions for homogeneous transforms, twists, adjoints and extraction of R and p.

atoms.idea: Homogeneous representation makes the package easy to combine with other symbolic tools.
atoms.feynman: Standard-size plugs fit every socket.
atoms.visual: Bench gadgets snap together by matching 4-slot connectors.

atoms.idea: Group one covers rotation matrices: all operations of Chapter 2 §2 on SO(3).
atoms.feynman: The first drawer holds everything for spinning things.
atoms.visual: SO(3) drawer opens: a row of four gadget boxes with spin icons.

atoms.idea: SO(3) functions: vector → skew matrix (hat); rotation matrix → its rotation axis; exponential of a skew matrix with optional angle (default 1; accepts a vector directly); skew matrix → vector (vee).
atoms.feynman: Four gadgets: turn an arrow into a spin-maker, find the spin axis of a turned ball, spin by an amount, and turn a spin-maker back into an arrow.
atoms.visual: Drop an orange ω into hat → 3×3 skew tiles; feed tiles + θ slider into exp → a blue frame spins (Rodrigues); feed the frame into axis → the gold axis arrow returns; vee turns tiles back into ω (lime round-trip). Crucible: lie.hat, lie.logSO3 (axis = normalized log), lie.expSO3(ω·θ), lie.vee.

atoms.idea: Only light argument checking is performed.
atoms.feynman: The gadgets trust you to put in the right shape of thing.
atoms.visual: Feeding a non-skew matrix into vee shows a coral warning shake; Crucible scenes guard inputs by construction.

atoms.idea: Group two handles SE(3) with 4×4 matrices: converting points and vectors to/from homogeneous form and building a matrix from (R, p).
atoms.feynman: The second drawer holds everything for picking things up and putting them somewhere else.
atoms.visual: SE(3) drawer opens: gadget boxes with move icons; R and p pieces snap into a 4×4 frame.

atoms.idea: SE(3) functions (part 1): 4×4 twist matrix → 6-vector; point → homogeneous (append 1); g → 6×6 adjoint; extract R from g; extract p from g; twist generating a given g (matrix log).
atoms.feynman: Gadgets that take a "move" apart: which way it turns, where it ends up, its 6-number recipe, and how it re-describes other twists.
atoms.visual: Feed a pink frame g in: outputs R (blue block), p (teal arrow), the twist ξ (gold screw, via log) and the 6×6 Ad tiles. Crucible: twist vee (NEW: twistVee), point→[q,1], lie.adjoint, lie.rotOf, lie.transOf, lie.logSE3.

atoms.idea: Page 436

pages.summary: Remaining SE(3) functions: (R,p) → matrix, screw → twist (with infinite pitch), twist axis, twist exponential, pitch, magnitude, conversions; then the companion package for manipulator kinematics via product of exponentials.

atoms.idea: Build a 4×4 homogeneous matrix from R and p.
atoms.feynman: Snap a turn and a shift together into one move card.
atoms.visual: Blue R block + teal p arrow slide into the 4×4 frame (lie.homog).

atoms.idea: Screw (pitch h, point q, direction ω) → twist coordinates; infinite pitch gives a pure translation along ω, ignoring q.
atoms.feynman: Describe a bolt by where its axis is and how coarse its thread is; an infinitely coarse thread just slides.
atoms.visual: Gold axis through draggable q with ω; pitch dial; output twist bars. Turning the dial to ∞ morphs the motion to pure slide and q's handle greys out. Crucible: lie.screwAxis(ω, q, h); pure slide as [0,0,0,ω].

atoms.idea: Twist → its screw axis as (point q, unit direction ω); accepts a 6-vector or a 4×4.
atoms.feynman: Given how a bolt is moving, find the line it is turning around.
atoms.visual: Feed a twist; the gold axis line and a teal foot point q (closest to origin, q = ω×v/‖ω‖²) appear.

atoms.idea: Matrix exponential of a twist with optional θ (default 1), accepting 6-vectors.
atoms.feynman: Run the bolt-turning motion for θ seconds and see where the part ends up.
atoms.visual: Twist + θ slider → a frame corkscrews along the axis (lie.expSE3(ξ·θ)).

atoms.idea: Pitch of a twist (ωᵀv/‖ω‖²) and magnitude (‖ω‖, or ‖v‖ for pure translation).
atoms.feynman: How far the bolt advances per turn, and how fast it turns.
atoms.visual: Pitch dial and magnitude bar read off any twist dropped in (NEW: twistPitch, twistMagnitude).

atoms.idea: Twist 6-vector → 4×4 matrix; vector → homogeneous (append 0).
atoms.feynman: Write the bolt recipe in matrix form; arrows get a 0 so they don't get shifted.
atoms.visual: 6 twist bars fold into 4×4 tiles (NEW: twistHat); an orange arrow gets a 0 slot and only rotates when multiplied.

atoms.idea: Again only light argument checking.
atoms.feynman: Same trust rule for the second drawer.
atoms.visual: Coral shake on a mis-shaped input.

atoms.idea: Subheading: manipulator kinematics.
The screw tools can analyze manipulators; a companion package adds helpers that streamline it.
atoms.feynman: With the screw gadgets you can now assemble whole robot arms.
atoms.visual: Bench switches to the arm-building drawer.

atoms.idea: Forward kinematics is a product of exponentials of joint twists; helpers create those twists.
atoms.feynman: Each joint adds its own twist, one after another, like turning dials in a row.
atoms.visual: An empty slate base with a tray of joint tokens.

atoms.idea: Page 437

pages.summary: Helpers for revolute and prismatic joint twists; forward kinematics and spatial Jacobian functions; a SCARA example builds four joint twists and a tool frame and computes the forward kinematics.

atoms.idea: Unit twists for a revolute joint (axis ω through q: (−ω×q, ω)) and a prismatic joint (direction ω: (ω, 0)), built from the screw-to-twist function.
atoms.feynman: A hinge is a bolt with zero thread; a sliding drawer is a bolt with infinite thread.
atoms.visual: Drop a revolute token: place q and ω → gold axis, twist bars appear (lie.screwAxis with h=0). Drop a prismatic token: an arrow → twist bars with zero spin.

atoms.idea: Given the twists, forward kinematics and the Jacobian follow from multiplying twist exponentials and applying adjoints; helper functions automate this.
atoms.feynman: Once each dial is labelled, the hand's place is just all dial turns applied in order.
atoms.visual: Joint sliders appear under the tokens; frames of each link appear as the exps are multiplied left to right.

atoms.idea: Forward kinematics from a list of (twist, angle) pairs and the home tool frame by the product of exponentials.
atoms.feynman: Turn every dial by its amount, in order, then put the hand where it sits at home and see where it ends up.
atoms.visual: Drag θ sliders (orange); the pink tool frame moves; a ghost of the home configuration stays visible (kinematics.poeFK(screws, M, θ)).

atoms.idea: Spatial manipulator Jacobian from the same inputs.
atoms.feynman: For each dial, how the hand would start moving if only that dial turned.
atoms.visual: 6×n tile panel: column i lights up as the current (Ad-transformed) twist of joint i; wiggling one slider shows that column's motion (kinematics.spaceJacobian).

atoms.idea: A worked example computes SCARA kinematics with Chapter-2 notation.
atoms.feynman: Let's build the classic pick-and-place table robot.
atoms.visual: Preset button loads the SCARA arm onto the base.

atoms.idea: The example loads both packages, defines three vertical revolute twists through (0,0,0), (0,l₁,0), (0,l₁+l₂,0) and one vertical prismatic twist, places the tool at (0, l₁+l₂, 0) with identity orientation, and simplifies the product-of-exponentials forward map.
atoms.feynman: Three hinges standing upright in a row along the arm, plus a vertical slider at the end, like a desk lamp that can only swing flat and drop down.
atoms.visual: SCARA preset: three gold vertical axes at 0, l₁, l₁+l₂ and a vertical slide; pink tool at the arm tip; dragging θ₁–θ₃ sweeps the tool in a horizontal plane and θ₄ lowers it; the 4×4 readout shows the symbolic pattern (cos/sin of summed angles).

atoms.idea: Page 438

pages.summary: The SCARA example ends by computing and simplifying the spatial Jacobian.

atoms.idea: The example then computes and simplifies the SCARA spatial Jacobian from the same joint list.
atoms.feynman: Ask each of the four dials how it nudges the hand right now.
atoms.visual: SCARA Jacobian panel: four columns; the rows for tilting about x and y stay dark (zero), showing SCARA can only yaw and move in x, y, z.
